root_cause.text: The `CQE_F_MASK` macro in `io_uring/net.c` omitted `IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE`, causing that flag to be dropped when merging cflags during bundle recv retries in `io_recv_finish()`, which resulted in userspace incorrectly advancing the buffer ring head past an entry still in use by the kernel.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE` to the `CQE_F_MASK` define (line change from `#define CQE_F_MASK (IORING_CQE_F_SOCK_NONEMPTY|IORING_CQE_F_MORE)` to including `| IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE`). The commit message explains: "Because IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE was not in CQE_F_MASK, the merge above silently dropped it whenever the final retry iteration partially consumed the buffer, and the subsequent req->cqe.flags = cflags & ~CQE_F_MASK save would have left a stale IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE in the carried-over cflags had one been present. Userspace would then wrongfully advance it ring head past an entry the kernel still uses."

intent_record.intent_summary: Include IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE in the CQE flags mask for bundle retry to ensure proper flag handling.
intent_record.what: Added IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE flag to the CQE_F_MASK macro using a line continuation, changing the mask from two flags to three.
intent_record.how: The macro CQE_F_MASK is used to clear and inherit CQE flags on bundle retry. Including IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE ensures that this flag is also cleared/inherited correctly during retry operations, affecting behavior when buffer selection is involved.

vuln_statements.explanation: This macro definition omits IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE from the mask, so when merging cflags during bundle recv retries in io_recv_finish(), the BUF_MORE flag is dropped. This causes userspace to incorrectly advance the buffer ring head past an entry still in use by the kernel, violating the buffer ring protocol.
